recipes.name: Baked BBQ Chicken with Sweet Potato and Cranberries
ingredients_raw: 2 (5 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking dish.
Pierce sweet potato several times with a fork, then cut in half. Place in a microwave-safe dish; pour in about 1/2 inch of water. Microwave on high for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop carrots, apple, and onion; arrange in the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Brush barbecue sauce on both sides of the chicken breasts and lay atop the vegetables.
Remove sweet potato from the microwave. Peel and discard skin. Cut sweet potato into large chunks; scatter into the baking dish. Sprinkle cranberries over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is tender and no longer pink in the center, 45 to 55 minutes. Remove from the oven and allow to cool for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked BBQ Chicken with Sweet Potato and Cranberries
raw_recipe.description: Baked BBQ chicken breasts are cooked with sweet potatoes and cranberries in this sweet and savory meal for two that's perfect for dinner on a cold winter night.

review.reviewBody: I've prepared this recipe a number of times, and I've made some changes that we think improved it. First, I omit the sweet potato (we don't like them). I add one chopped apple for each person (instead of one apple/two persons). I use baby carrots and cook them on the stove until they're about halfway cooked through, then drain them and toss them with the chopped apples. I omit the onion because it upsets our stomachs, but I season the apples and carrots with onion powder and pepper. A few times, I've added small red potatoes that I've quartered (depending on size) and tossed with the seasoned apples and carrots, but the last time I made this I baked potatoes (not sweet potatoes) to serve alongside. One thing I do now that I think is crucial to making this dish moist is to add some apple juice approximately halfway through baking. I pour it into the apple/carrot/potato (if using) mix in the bottom of the pan and stir it around. I check it again about 10 minutes later and add more juice, if needed. This keeps everything from drying out. I also use dried cranberries instead of fresh, and the apple juice helps a lot with 'plumping' them. All in all, both my husband and I really enjoy this dish in the winter. It's easy to prepare and compared to many other recipes, fairly healthy.

I couldn’t sleep because I kept thinking of how good my small serving of this was so I went downstairs and heated up another small serving! Note: I didn’t have bbq sauce so I used Garlic Teriyaki sauce. I already had baked sweet potatoes I used one, next time I’ll use 1 and a half. I used 4 small carrots, next time more carrots , 1 cup of cranberries sounded like too much. I reduced to 1/2 cup and that was just right. I also added more salt, pepper, plus smoked paprika. I removed from oven after 40 minutes, thermopop temp was 140. I left it sit now covered with foil for 10 minutes and it was cooked perfectly inside, moist, juicy. I’m always looking to cook just enough to be safe but not overcooked.

This was delicious, and the family loved it! I microwaved a couple of sweet potatoes until about half done and steamed the onion wedges and carrots until half done. Then put carrots, onions, and apple on the bottom. Seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper and dredged both sides in about a half cup of bar-b-q sauce before putting on top of the vegetables. Scattered the chunks of sweet potato then topped it all with a cup of fresh cranberries cooked in a 1/3 C of O.J. and about 1/8 C sugar until they popped. Covered with foil and it was all done and ready to eat in about an hour. The chicken was moist and the whole dish was delicious! I'm going to try it again with boneless skinless chicken thighs.

This was pretty good! I chopped the vegetables, put them in a large bowl, added some olive oil and balsamic vinegar, about 1 teas of salt and 1 teas of pepper, and 2 T rosemary. Tossed them, and roasted the vegetables at 400 degrees for 30 minutes. I used 1/4 cup apple juice, 1/4 cup chicken broth, and 1/2 cup barbeque sauce and added 1 teas garlic powder. I chopped up my chicken into bite sized pieces. I mixed everything together, and put it in a 9 x 13 pan. I baked it covered with foil for 30 minutes at 375, but the carrots were still hard. So I baked it covered another 30 minutes and it was just right. Very tasty. This made a LOT of vegetables, so next time I'll double the chicken to 4 breasts instead of 2. The recipe as is made enough for 4, so I'd like the additional chicken in it.

Like most others, I made some adjustments. I added 1/2 cup of chicken broth for moisture, and added a little seasoning to the vegetables (nutmeg and a dash of cinnamon) which added to the winter flavor of the dish. I also added a red onion and green bell peppers. Lastly, I covered the dish with foil for the first 30 minutes, then added additional bbq sauce when I removed it. Absolutely Delicious!

I tried this and thought it was Boring! So my family had to eat it 2 days in a row. First I seasoned my chicken with salt and pepper and left on the counter for 30 minutes. Then I chopped sweet 2 potatoes 1 yellow onion and roasted them in my baking pan for 15 minutes. Added carrots and shallots and roasted 15 more minutes. Added chicken and spread with olive oil then sprinkled with Thyme and about 1/3 cup of white wine, baked for 40 minutes. It was Fabulous! But I couldn’t have done this without your roadmap. Cheers

I took the advice of other reviewers and adjusted the seasoning. I tossed the cut up vegetables with olive oil and dusted them with cinnamon. As I was putting this all together, it occured to me that everything there would be better with cinnamon. Instead of leaving the chicken breasts intact, I cut them into pieces, thoroughly coated them with barbecue sauce, and mixed the pieces into the vegetables before cooking. I also increased the amount of chicken (approx 18 oz) and the amount of sweet potato (one large) to make this into four servings. I didn't add any salt. It would have helped, but I am on a low sodium diet. The sweet potato didn't need to be pre-cooked. I was perfectly cooked at 45 minutes. My wife and I enjoyed the dish and I will probably make it again.

We really enjoyed this meal. I started with frozen chicken breasts and inserted a meat thermometer to 165 degrees. The chicken was very moist and perfect. I did add about3/4 cup of Apple Cider to the veggies and a can of whole cranberries. I forgot to precook the carrots, so they were crunchie. I served it over Quiona, brown and red rice microwave side. I saved/froze the leftover veggies to use maybe for pork chops another time. I will definitely make again...two thumbs up!

This recipe is pretty awful as-is. How can you have no salt or seasoning or oil with root vegetables? I also don't understand why the sweet potato needed to be cooked in the microwave- chop it up with everything else. 45 minutes is plenty long to cook the sweet potato, and it won't be an unappetizing mush. Toss the veggies in olive oil, kosher salt, and pepper. Toss the chicken in Ms dash or Montreal seasoning, and add bbq sauce if you like your chicken sweet. Add a splash of apple cider vinegar or lemon juice. Now you have yourself a salvageable recipe.

Very good recipe. Took the suggestion of adding a little apple juice for moisture. I also added a 1/4 cup chicken broth, garlic and 1/2 tsp thyme. I used dried cranberries and placed under the chicken breasts. They really plumped up. The apple juice and chicken broth gave me a nice gravy.

I thought this recipe was oddly appealing, so I decided to try it. However I immediately converted it to crockpot because I had no desire to cook things separately. 

Skipped carrots, put onions, diced sweet potatoes, frozen cranberries (I discovered not I, not 2,but 3 partial bags of cranberries in my freezer). Also added a cup of apple cider. I cooked them on high for two hours because I know how long it takes to cook sweet potatoes. After 2 hours, I added chopped apple, then boneless chicken thighs slathered with BBQ sauce on top. Cooked all 5 more hours on high cuz the thighs were partially frozen.

Totally delicious and moist. Will make again.
It seemed healthy and yet fun! A perfect contribution to a Christmas or fall party! Everything was included. My son rated it a 13 out of 10!

PROCEDURE: No microwave! I pre-boiled my carrots for ten minutes and my cut up sweet potato for five. Maybe it's the time of year, but my carrots are tough. I would modify those numbers for the veggies on hand. Next time I'm going to take a tip from my fellow cooks and put my dried cranberries under the chicken. I baked it for 35 minutes... Next time I will check it starting at 25. I have tenderloin in my freezer. I didn't add water because my veg was quite plump from the parboiling. This awesome recipe for using up food bank supplies is going to get even better!
Very good!! I was a little nervous that it would be sweet, but it wasn’t at all. I will definitely be making it again!!

Delicious! I added paprika, pepper, and a little salt and sugar. I also added the apple juice (I didn't measure, it covered the bottom of the casserole dish) and covered it with aluminum foil to bake. I had boneless skinless chicken thighs, so I checked the temp after 45 minutes and it was 155-160 degrees. Lots of “sauce” generated, which was delicious with the veggies. Had a small amount of veggies left for the two of us. Amount was perfect.

Pretty good, simple. I used fresh cranberries. Cubed the sweet potato and put it in to bake from the beginning. I didn't use carrots but will if I make this again. May add an extra apple as suggested by another review.
The flavor was incredible! Certainly one we will make again.

I wish I had used a third chicken breast. The dish is delicious and rather healthy in my opinion. The cranberries do nothing for the dish. It doesn't add anything to taste or texture. I'll leave it out next time and save me a little bit of dough!

This is delicious! Even my picky daughter liked it. I only made a few changes such as adding olive oil and salt to the veggies and chicken and reducing the amount of dried cranberries to a half a cup. I will make this again.
